reason: Verified in source and by driving the page. render-b.js move() (lines ~229-238) writes only data-away, item.style.top, .b-away and read.textContent; .b-date and the .b-grab aria-label are written once in measure() at render and never touched again. Live DOM at 1440x960, owner-editing, after one click of −7: .b-away = "16", .b-date = "Sat 8 Aug", .b-grab aria-label = "Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests. Open to change it.", .b-stepRead = "in 16 days" — four statements of one fact, three of them false, on the one gesture this direction exists for. The readout also opens as "Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days" and drops the calendar date permanently on first touch, so the owner moving a wedding milestone is never again told which date they landed on. The .b-undo live region ships pre-written with "Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer." before any interaction and is still that exact string after two moves — a role=status region asserting a change that never happened. The gate is genuinely vacuous here: interaction-check.mjs line 310 tests only readout.includes(String(moved.away)), so a bare "in 16 days" passes while the date line and the accessible name are stale. Not taste, not a constraint breach, not a restatement. One measurement the finding missed strengthens it: because the readout collapses from 346.5px to 99px, the .b-stepRow unwraps and the +1/+7 buttons jump 209px horizontally (x 751→960) between clicks, so the control you are repeating moves out from under the cursor. Restoring the full string fixes that too.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as written for the date derivation — add addDays inside fixture.js's IIFE (where utc() is in scope) and expose it on the api object, then in move() derive one iso = F.addDays(target.date, current - away) using the closure's original away, and from that single value rewrite .b-away, .b-date (F.fmt.weekdayShort + ' ' + F.fmt.short), the .b-grab aria-label and read.textContent (F.fmt.longYear(iso) + ' · in ' + current + ' days') in the same frame. Two corrections. (1) The undo half as written breaks a passing gate: interaction-check.mjs already asserts "it says what it would undo" via /moved|change/i on .b-undo textContent at load, and an empty sentence fails it ('Undo' and 'Ctrl Z' match neither word). Keep the .b-undo row rendered (three other assertions require it to exist, be singular and carry a control plus a key), render the sentence span empty and the Undo button disabled until the first move, then write the sentence and enable the button from the same move; and move that existing assertion to run after the move rather than at load, adding the new empty-before-interaction assertion at load. (2) Give .b-stepRead a min-width in ch (roughly 24ch at the desk size) so the row cannot unwrap and reflow the +1/+7 buttons between clicks. Then replace line 310's assertion with one that parses .b-date, the .b-grab aria-label and .b-stepRead and requires all three to name the date implied by .b-away.
